title: India enterprise private launch sprint brief
content:
Objective:

Prepare a concise, action-oriented launch pack for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) targeted at India enterprise buyers (FSI, telecom, public sector, large SaaS). This doc is the working sprint brief for marketing, sales enablement, partner ops, and solutions engineering.

Context / Why now:
- Increasing interest from India enterprises for private inference due to data residency, regulatory constraints, and IP protection.
- Several inbound RFPs in the last quarter explicitly ask for VPC/on-prem options, HSM/KMS integrations, and auditability.
- Competitors (both cloud marketplaces and local integrators) are packaging inference as managed appliances — we need a clear enterprise message that emphasizes predictable economics + developer-first experience.

Target personas and use cases (priority order):
1) Head of AI / ML Platform (large SaaS / fintech) — needs predictable latency, quota controls across product teams, model versioning, and SLOs.
2) CTO / VP Eng (regulated finance, payments) — concerned about data residency, compliance, and vendor support SLAs.
3) Product security/compliance lead — KMS/HSM, audit logs, access controls, contractual controls.
4) Solutions/Platform engineers (implementation buyers) — need smooth installation, Kubernetes integrations, OIDC/SAML, and clear rollback/upgrade procedures.

Key positioning pillars (core messages):
- Production-first inference in your network: Redwood Private brings the same developer experience as our hosted API but within your VPC or on-prem environment.
- Predictable economics + capacity controls: Reserved pools, autoscale policies, and Intelligent batching reduce token cost while preserving latency SLAs.
- Enterprise-grade compliance and controls: KMS/HSM options, audit trails, RBAC, and private control plane for regulated workloads.
- One operational model across environments: single API, model pinning, rollouts, and observability whether hosted or private.

Value props (short bullets for outbound):
- Keep your data in-region and under your control — deploy Redwood Private in your VPC or dedicated on-prem instance.
- Move fast with developer-friendly APIs and SDKs identical to our hosted cloud experience.
- Guarantee throughput and latency with dedicated pools and SLA-backed targets.
- Reduce unit cost using batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations tailored to your workloads.

Competitive landscape (India-specific notes):
- Global cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure): Strength is managed infra and marketplace reach. Typical objection: lock-in and lack of inference optimizations for open models. Our counters: vendor-agnostic runtime optimizations, model catalog tuned for performance, and playbook for partner-managed installs on their cloud accounts.
- Local system integrators / managed service providers: They bundle open-source runtimes + consulting. Strength: local presence and custom contracts. Our counters: productized private offering, Redwood Console for observability, and partner enablement kits so SI can deliver faster with standardized packages.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes (open-source projects) and inference startups: Strength: low-cost, flexible. Weakness: operational burden, limited rollout/rollout safety. Our counters: SLA, maintenance, rollout tools (canary/A-B), and dedicated support.

Pricing and packaging (draft):
- Private Starter: small single-cluster on VPC, monthly support, best for PoCs (3–6 month).
- Private Reserved: dedicated pools, monthly commit + overage pricing, advanced support.
- Private Enterprise: multi-region on-prem/VPC, HSM/KMS integrations, compliance package, named SLAs and SSO.
(Exact numbers TBD — coordinate with commercial ops)

Launch motions and partner plays:
- Channel-first for large integrators: identify 3 partners with existing Gov/FSI relationships for co-sell pilots. Prepare partner pack: technical install guide, SOW template, partner enablement webinar.
- Field enablement: sales playbook + battlecards for top 10 objection scenarios.
- Developer activation: Private quickstart repo with sample infra-as-code for common Indian cloud accounts and a PoC checklist to go from 0 -> 1 in 48 hours.
- Events & PR: local webinars co-hosted with a partner on ‘inference at the edge with compliance’.

Sales enablement artifacts to create (sprint deliverables):
- 1-pager: Redwood Private value for India enterprises (external).
- Battlecard: Redwood vs. local SI, cloud, open-source (internal).
- Technical runbook: install checklist, upgrade path, rollback steps (SE-facing).
- Demo script: 10-minute demo showing model pinning, rollout, and cost dashboard (for AE/SE).
- Email + SLACK templates: launch announcement for customers and internal GTM.

Sample customer-facing launch announcement (draft):
Subject: Introducing Redwood Private — enterprise-grade LLM inference inside your VPC

We’re excited to announce Redwood Private, a deployment option that delivers Redwood’s high-performance inference inside your network. For Indian enterprises with strict data residency or compliance needs, Redwood Private provides the same developer-focused API and console you already know, with additional controls for security, auditing, and dedicated capacity.

Key benefits:
- Keep data in-region and under your control
- Predictable latency and cost with dedicated pools and autoscale policies
- Enterprise controls: KMS/HSM, RBAC, audit logs

If you’re interested in a technical conversation or a pilot, reply to this email and we’ll connect you with our solutions engineering team.

Internal launch Slack post (draft):
Title: [GT-MKT] India — Redwood Private launch sprint kicked off
Body: Heads up GTM & SE — we’re launching a regional push for Redwood Private targeting FSI / telco / large SaaS. Primary asks: 1) Sales — prioritize inbound RFPs that require VPC/on-prem. 2) SEs — please run the install playbook with partners in sandbox. Links: (partner pack) (SE runbook). Ping @Rajat or @Asha for questions.

Objection handling (top 8):
1) "Too complex to install / maintain" — We provide standardized install manifests, partner-managed installs, and a Redwood-backed support tier for PB.
2) "Vendor lock / model portability" — API compatible runtime and tooling for moving models; we support model export and common weight formats.
3) "Cost concerns vs. open-source" — Show TCO: engineer ops hours + time-to-LLM-quality + cost per inference with caching/batching.
4) "Compliance/legal requirements" — We have KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and can provide SOC2/ISO artifacts; escalation path to legal.
5) "Integration with internal identity and networking" — OIDC/SAML, VPC peering, private enrollment docs available.
6) "Latency guarantees" — Dedicated pools and SLOs; runbook for capacity planning and burst policies.
7) "Model freshness/versioning" — Model catalog + version pinning + rollout controls.
8) "Support SLAs in India timezones" — Local support on call for enterprise contracts; partner-managed field teams.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 3 signed pilot agreements with FSI / telco customers
- 2 channel partners onboarded and enabled with partner packs
- >50 SE-led installs in sandbox environments
- Customer survey NPS >= 7 for pilot ease-of-use

Launch timeline (high-level sprint):
- Week 0 (this doc): align GTM, draft assets, partner shortlist.
- Week 1: finalize pricing outline, publish 1-pager, record demo.
- Week 2: partner webinars, SE enablement sessions, start first pilot installs.
- Week 3–6: iterate on feedback, address blockers, close pilots / convert to reserved contracts.

Open questions (action owners):
- Legal: standard contract templates for data residency and on-prem support (owner: Lina).
- Pricing: confirmed commit tiers for India pricing and currency (owner: Samir).
- Partner ops: shortlist of 6 partners and POC contacts (owner: Rajat).
- Tech: finalize HSM integration checklist and sample KMS config (owner: Maya).

Appendix: quick battlecard highlights (one-liners)
- vs Global cloud provider: We deliver a vendor-agnostic, inference-optimized runtime that reduces per-token cost and gives consistent latency across model variants.
- vs Local SI: We provide a repeatable, productized private deployment with console-based observability and standardized partner playbooks.
- vs OSS runtimes: We add SLA-backed operations, rollout safety, and first-class developer tooling so teams ship faster.

Notes to self / rough ideas to capture later:
- Consider small pre-packaged OVA for partner field installs where VPC isn't allowed.
- Create a short checklist for data classification and guidance for customers to map data types to retention rules.
- Draft one-pager for compliance teams summarizing SOC2/ISO and typical audit artifacts.
- Evaluate running a 3-customer pilot sprint with partner for co-marketing case studies.
